notes: Fictional subject and object (moved from 0001): a nonce noun ('wug' style) and its nonce plural in the real relation singular_of, with a goose-style plural. Determinate queries compare it with real nouns (Q1) and build a compound's plural on it (Q2), the one route in each. Indeterminate queries are the aggregate case of README, Insert: closed lists of real nouns ('foot, goose, tooth'; 'goose' alone among '-oose' nouns) that the new noun joins if the model recomputes them and does not join if it stores them as facts. Q3 leaves out compounds (forefoot, eyetooth); Q4 leaves out compounds of 'goose' (Canada goose, snow goose: plural in -geese) and says 'standard' plural because 'mongeese' and 'meese' are jocular (Wikipedia). Near query asks the real 'moose', so a leak ('meese' by analogy) is caught. Grammar ABox may have all derived queries determinate; this record keeps the 2+2 shape it was written with (subject_object inserts may have 0 or 2 indeterminate queries).
